chunks: Al-Mudaffar ibn Ja'far ibn al-Mudaffar al-Alawi, may Allah be pleased with him, told us: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Mas'ud told us, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Ahmad, who said: Al-'Amari told me, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both), who said:

Tabattul is that you turn your palms during supplication when you supplicate. Ibtihal is that you extend them and bring them forward. Raghba is that you face the sky with your palms and face them with your face. Rahba is that you incline your palms by raising them to the face. Tadharru' is that you move your two fingers and point with them. And in another narration: Basbasa is that you raise your index fingers to the sky, move them and supplicate.

key_terms.التُّضْرُعُ: Moving the two fingers and pointing with them
key_terms.الرَّغْبَةُ: Facing the sky with the palms and the face
key_terms.الرَّهْبَةُ: Inclining the palms while raising them to the face
key_terms.الِابْتِهَال: Extending and bringing forward the palms
key_terms.الْبَصْبَصَةُ: Raising and moving the index fingers while supplicating

ai.seo_question: What are the different meanings of hand gestures in Shia supplication etiquette?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq meticulously categorizes the somatic expressions of humility in supplication, linking specific hand postures to distinct spiritual states such as hope (Raghba) and awe (Rahba). This classification reflects the Shia emphasis on the harmony between physical action and inner devotion, where gestures like raising palms or moving fingers serve as tangible manifestations of the soul's engagement with the Divine. The inclusion of 'Basbasa' highlights the nuanced tradition of using index fingers to direct focus upward, reinforcing the connection between bodily movement and spiritual intent.
